translation_notes: prefixes: foaf->http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/, rdfs->http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema# (FOAF-the-import retired from the draft: the only thing it fed was the runtime `% FOAF` splice, gone once the prefix is `@prefix`-static, so keeping the import would leave a dead binding and falsify the surface diff).

THE actual sparql_interpolated site (line 62 of the source): `g.query("PREFIX foaf: <%s> SELECT * WHERE { ?s a foaf:Agent . }" % FOAF)`. The interpolation builds the query's PROLOGUE (a PREFIX declaration), not a term inside a triple pattern -- so it is not `s{ }`'s `{expr}` term-interpolation that replaces it, it is `@prefix foaf: <http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/> .` (declared once, lexically, at transpile time) making the runtime PREFIX clause unnecessary altogether: `s{ SELECT * WHERE { ?s a foaf:Agent . } }(g)`, no interpolation left to write. Verified by transpiling in isolation: the generated code calls `_ldpy_.prepared('SELECT * WHERE { ?s a foaf:Agent . }', (), __namespaces__, ...)` -- the PREFIX text is gone, prefix resolution happens through __namespaces__ instead. This is the strongest form of 'directly-expressible' this stratum offers: the interpolation is not relocated, it disappears.

the isolated `g.add((FOAF.Person, rdflib.RDFS.subClassOf, FOAF.Agent))` (not itself interpolated -- add_isolated shape, same file) became `@graph g` + `+{ foaf:Person rdfs:subClassOf foaf:Agent }`, the more specific construction over the draft's `g += g{ ... }` (which built a whole second graph just to union it back in for one triple).

NOT-EXPRESSIBLE, and deliberately left as plain, untouched Python on both sides: `customEval`/`inferredSubClass`/`CUSTOM_EVALS`. This is not a graph read or write -- it registers a custom evaluator into rdflib's OWN SPARQL algebra engine (`rdflib.plugins.sparql.evaluate.evalBGP`), rewriting `part.triples` (algebra-level (s,p,o) tuples, `p` sometimes a Path object built with `RDFS.subClassOf * "*"`) before delegating back to evalBGP. No island models 'intercept how the query engine itself evaluates a BGP': islands write/read graphs and queries, they do not reach into the evaluator that runs them. Confirmed by the language reference table (SS1 of INSTRUCTIONS.md) having no construct for algebra-node rewriting at all.

EXCLUDED at the whole-region level, for a reason unrelated to translation quality: the graph-touching code (`g.load`, the add, the query) sits inside `if __name__ == "__main__":`. rdfeval.harness executes both files with `__name__` set to `"__original__"`/`"__translated__"` (never `"__main__"`), so that block never runs on EITHER side under run_pair -- confirmed: `rdfeval check` reports FAIL, diff 'nothing observable to compare', not a crash. Left the guard untouched rather than rewriting it to `if True:` or similar: original.py must mirror the corpus source, and INSIDE that guard there is a SECOND, independent blocker anyway -- `g.load("foaf.n3")` fails identically on both sides even run directly (`python -m ldpy translated.ldpy`, where __name__ genuinely is __main__): `Graph.load` does not exist on rdflib 7.2.1 (confirmed: `hasattr(Graph(), 'load')` is False -- an API rdflib actually removed, not a typo), and 'foaf.n3' is not shipped anywhere in this corpus clone even if `.load` still existed. See driver.py for the full chain.

what step 3 of the protocol (transpile) DOES confirm, independent of the __main__/foaf.n3 blockers: `python -m ldpy translated.ldpy` and a standalone `ldpy.transpiler.transpile()` call both succeed -- the `@prefix`, `+{ }` and `s{ }` islands are syntactically valid, and the `s{ }` query's SPARQL text parses (querying.md: parsed at transpile time, not run time) -- so the translation itself is sound; only its EXECUTION is blocked, by the file's own pre-existing dependency on rdflib's old `.load` API and a missing local fixture file, both inherited unchanged from the corpus source.
